feed.title: Design term of the day · Follow or Bounce
feed.subtitle: One term a day from the Dictionary of Design.

entry.title: Gradient
entry.summary: A continuous, stepless transition between two visual states — most often color, value, or scale.

entry.title: Rhythm
entry.summary: Visual tempo produced by repeating elements with controlled variation in spacing, size, or form.

entry.title: Prototype
entry.summary: An interactive or tangible model of a design used to test its functionality, flow, and user experience.

entry.title: API
entry.summary: An interface enabling one piece of software to interact with another — adjacent professional vocabulary a designer encounters, not a design concept in its own right.

entry.title: Unity
entry.summary: The degree to which elements read as belonging to one coherent whole rather than as unrelated parts.

entry.title: Module
entry.summary: A single repeatable unit whose form determines the structure and proportions of a larger composition.

entry.title: Abstraction
entry.summary: Progressive simplification of a recognizable form into essential geometric shape, retaining what makes it identifiable while discarding surface detail.

entry.title: Wireframe
entry.summary: A simplified visual guide showing a layout's structure and hierarchy without detailed styling.

entry.title: Plasticity
entry.summary: The degree to which a form reads as pliable or moldable rather than rigid, judged from its contours and transitions.

entry.title: Frontend / Backend
entry.summary: The two halves of a digital system: frontend is what a user sees, backend is the server-side logic and data behind it — adjacent professional vocabulary.

entry.title: Scale
entry.summary: Perceived size, understood only through comparison against another object or a known reference, not as an absolute measure.

entry.title: Tectonics
entry.summary: The expressive articulation of a structure's logic through the treatment of its surface and form.

entry.title: API
entry.summary: An interface enabling one piece of software to interact with another — adjacent professional vocabulary a designer encounters, not a design concept in its own right.

entry.title: Unity
entry.summary: The degree to which elements read as belonging to one coherent whole rather than as unrelated parts.

entry.title: Typography System
entry.summary: The organized use of typefaces, styles, spacing, and hierarchy to communicate clearly and consistently across a project.

entry.title: Illustration Pack
entry.summary: A collection of related illustrations sharing one style and thematic language, used consistently across a project.

entry.title: Visual Identity
entry.summary: The visual components of a brand or project — logo, color palette, typography, and imagery — forming one recognizable system.

entry.title: PDF
entry.summary: Portable Document Format — preserves a document's layout, typography, and graphics identically across platforms.

entry.title: Legibility
entry.summary: Whether individual letterforms can be told apart from one another at a glance.

entry.title: Collage
entry.summary: A technique of combining diverse, often unrelated visual fragments into one new, unified composition.

entry.title: Rhythm
entry.summary: Visual tempo produced by repeating elements with controlled variation in spacing, size, or form.

entry.title: Brandbook
entry.summary: A comprehensive document defining a project's visual identity, typography, color palette, and guidelines for consistent application.

entry.title: Composition
entry.summary: The spatial and proportional organization of elements into a coherent whole.

entry.title: Light
entry.summary: The degree of illumination defining an object's visibility, and its contrast against surrounding darkness.

entry.title: Raster
entry.summary: A pixel-based image format whose detail is fixed at capture or creation, distinguished from RAW by not necessarily being an unprocessed camera file.

entry.title: Grading (Career Grading)
entry.summary: A structured system defining professional levels, responsibilities, and skill growth within a discipline.

entry.title: CMS
entry.summary: A software platform for creating, managing, and publishing digital content — adjacent professional vocabulary.

entry.title: Composition
entry.summary: The spatial and proportional organization of elements into a coherent whole.

entry.title: Affordance
entry.summary: A property of a form's shape that suggests, on its own, how it is meant to be used.

entry.title: Digital Toolkit
entry.summary: The suite of software, templates, and resources used to create, edit, and manage a digital design project — absorbs what the source separately, redundantly, called Graphic Editor.
